answer: A wander is not a plan, so the ledger prices distance. An identity must register a karst route whose every waypoint two holders outside its own cluster notarize, and one waypoint may anchor only one traveller, so n aliases need n distinct notaries and cannot share a single itinerary. Each route is sealed with an onyx receipt that records its notaries, and the k-th sealing an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed. An audit re-walks a random waypoint; an unconfirmed one voids the entire karst route and its bonds, so purchased testimony buys nothing.
